transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Well, I suppose what brings me in is… I just can’t seem to turn the worrying off once it gets going. I’ll tell myself, “I’ve made the list, I checked the dates, I’ve done what I can,” you know, the sensible things. I’ve always been a list person—my husband used to tease me about having lists for my lists—but lately it doesn’t settle me the way it should. The worry just keeps circling back anyway.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different things, even when there isn't a clear reason to be concerned about them?

Yes, I do. It sort of hops around, if that makes sense. One minute I’m thinking about the exhibition schedule—there’s this small local art thing I help keep track of, or used to be better at keeping track of—and then suddenly I’m worrying about my daughter’s travel plans, whether she’ll make her connections, whether I should remind her about things she already knows.

And then it’ll be something like the gutters on the house, which I know sounds silly, but I’ll think, “If they’re not fixed, then water could get in, and then it becomes a whole ordeal.” Small things start feeling like they could unravel into something much bigger, even when nothing has actually happened.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms when you're feeling anxious, like restlessness, muscle tension, or trouble sleeping?

Yes… I do get that wound-up feeling. It’s funny, because it can happen when I’m just sitting in my own living room, which should be the calmest place, shouldn’t it? I’ll be on the phone and notice I’m tapping my fingers, or I’ll suddenly get up to straighten a stack of papers or adjust a picture frame—my mother used to do that before company came, everything at right angles—and then I realize I’m not tidying so much as I just can’t quite sit still. Sitting quietly makes me feel jumpy sometimes.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying and anxiety, and does it seem to happen more days than not?

I think… about seven months now. It started not long after my friend died, when I was trying to keep our little projects going—there were files and calls and all these loose ends, and I thought if I just stayed organized it would be fine.

But yes, it’s been more days than not, I’d say. It isn’t every single minute, but most days it finds something to latch onto.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you know it might not make sense?

Yes… that’s actually what brings me in, I think. Once the worrying starts, I have a very hard time turning it off, even when I know I’ve already done everything sensible—made the list, checked the dates, gone over whatever it is.

I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough now,” but then my mind goes right back to it. It’s like when you leave the house and wonder if you locked the door, except it’s not just the door, it’s the calendar, or a phone call, or something I said to someone. And I can know, logically, that it doesn’t really help to keep thinking about it… but knowing that doesn’t seem to stop it.
Have you ever experienced sudden episodes where you feel intense fear or discomfort that comes on very quickly, like your heart racing, shortness of breath, or feeling like you're losing control?

I don’t think so… not in that sudden, out-of-nowhere way you’re describing. I mean, I can get very worked up, but it feels more like it builds while I’m thinking and thinking.

My heart might feel like I’m aware of it, if that makes sense, but I don’t know that I’ve had an “attack” like people talk about. My neighbor used to say she had those in the grocery store—she’d leave a full cart right there by the oranges, poor thing. Mine isn’t really like that. It’s more… I’m already worrying, and then I’m uncomfortable.
Have you ever avoided certain places, situations, or activities because you were afraid they might trigger your anxiety or lead to something bad happening?

I’m not sure I’d say I avoid places exactly. I mean, I still go where I need to go. I’ve never been someone who loved crowds, but that’s not new—my sister used to drag me to those big holiday craft fairs, and I’d spend half the time looking at handmade soaps I didn’t need just to get a little space.

But… in terms of avoiding because I think something bad will happen, I don’t think so. I might put off a call or a task if I’m already wound up about it, but I don’t know if that counts as avoiding a place or activity the way you mean.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual or that you don't have the same energy you used to, even when you haven't been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Yes, I have noticed that. It’s not like I’ve been hauling furniture around or anything. Even on nights when I sleep all the way through, I can wake up feeling like I’ve already done half a day’s work.

And then I’ll do something ordinary, like water the garden beds—though the back ones do take longer because the hose kinks near the lilacs, which drives me mad—or I’ll sort through papers for book club, and afterward I need to sit down for a bit and sort of gather myself. It feels like I run out of energy sooner than I used to.
Have you found yourself feeling more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even over small things?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, no. I mean, little things can get under anyone’s skin, can’t they? Like when the kitchen drawer sticks because one spatula is lying the wrong way—my husband used to say there was always one guilty spatula in every house.

But lately… I’m not sure I’d call myself more irritable. I don’t think people around me would say I’m snapping at them or anything. Maybe I get a bit impatient with things, but not in a way that stands out to me.
Have you found it harder to focus or concentrate on things lately, like following conversations, reading, or finishing tasks?

I’m not sure. I mean, I can still read and follow things, as far as I can tell. Sometimes if there’s a lot going on, I’ll have to go back over a paragraph, but I’ve always done that with certain books—especially the ones my book club picks that have fourteen characters and three of them are named something similar.

Conversations… I don’t think I’m losing the thread in any big way. Though if someone is telling me a long story while I’m trying to remember whether I left the tea kettle on, then of course I might miss a bit. But harder to concentrate lately? I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, no.
Have you noticed any days when you feel down or sad, or when things just don’t seem to give you the same pleasure or interest they used to?

I don’t think so… not in the way you mean, anyway. I have quieter days, certainly, where I don’t feel especially lively, but I can still enjoy things.

Like, I was out by the roses the other morning—well, they’re not doing as well as they did last year, probably because I pruned them too late—and I still liked being out there. And I still go to book club, even if half the time we talk more about who brought the lemon bars than the actual book.

So no, I haven’t really noticed feeling down or losing interest in things. Not especially.
Do you have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep because you're too anxious or worried, even if it's not every night?

I’m not sure I’d say that, exactly. I mean, some nights I lie there a bit thinking about ordinary things—did I lock the back door, did I put the bins out, that sort of thing—but I don’t know that it’s because I’m too anxious or worried.

Sleep is funny anyway, isn’t it? My sister swears by those lavender sprays, but I tried one once and it just made the pillow smell like a gift shop. So… trouble sleeping from worry? I haven’t really noticed that as a pattern, no.

Do you find that your anxiety or worry tends to be ongoing and not limited to specific situations or events, such that you feel anxious about many different things most days, even when nothing particularly stressful is happening?

Yes… I suppose it does wander around like that. It’s not just one thing, like an appointment or some big problem. My mind sort of hops from the exhibition schedule—there’s always something that needs arranging there—to my daughter’s travel plans, and then suddenly I’m thinking about whether the gutters on the house need fixing.

And they’re small things, mostly, but in my head they start feeling like they could turn into something much bigger if I don’t keep an eye on them. Like one loose thread and the whole jumper comes apart, if that makes sense.
Have you ever had a moment where your heart suddenly raced, you felt short of breath, or you thought something terrible was going to happen, even when there was no real danger?

No… I don’t think I’ve had anything quite like that. I mean, my heart might thump a bit if I’m rushing up the stairs or if the phone rings at an odd hour—though half the time it’s just someone asking about loft insulation, which is ridiculous—but not suddenly out of nowhere.

I can get unsettled, certainly, but that “something terrible is happening right now” feeling… I don’t really recognize that. At least, not that I can remember.
Do you feel tired or low on energy most days, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly taxing?

Yes, I do, actually. Even if I’ve slept through the night, I can wake up feeling as if I’ve already done half a day’s work somehow.

It’s silly, because I’ll only do something small—water the garden beds, or sort through papers for book club—and then I need to sit down and sort of gather myself. Mind you, the garden hose has a mind of its own, so perhaps that should count as exercise. But yes… I do feel low on energy more than I’d like.
